name: Pangu
role: Creator giant who separated sky and earth
fun_fact: In the best-known version, Pangu grows ten feet taller every day so that the sky and earth can never close together again.

name: Nüwa
role: Primordial goddess who repaired the sky and shaped humans
symbols: the legs of a giant turtle
fun_fact: Nüwa is often shown holding a compass, while her consort Fuxi holds a square, together representing order in heaven and earth.

name: Gonggong
role: Water god whose battle broke the sky pillar
fun_fact: Gonggong is sometimes depicted with a human face and a snake's body, and his name is linked to catastrophic flooding.

name: Hou Yi
role: Master archer who shot down nine suns
fun_fact: Hou Yi's story changes with the teller: he can be a selfless hero, a grieving husband, or a ruler who becomes a tyrant.

name: Chang'e
role: Moon goddess who swallowed the elixir of immortality
fun_fact: The Mid-Autumn Festival is associated with Chang'e, and mooncakes are shared while families look for her figure in the moon.

name: Yu the Great
role: Flood hero and legendary founder of the Xia dynasty
symbols: the door he passed three times
fun_fact: The saying that Yu passed his own door three times without entering became a model of public duty in Chinese political thought.

name: Yinglong
role: Winged dragon who helped Yu trace river channels
symbols: a tail drawing channels in the earth
fun_fact: Yinglong means 'responsive dragon'; in some versions the dragon's tail becomes the map that Yu follows.

name: Nezha
role: Child warrior reborn in a lotus body
fun_fact: Nezha is often shown with flaming wheels under his feet and a spear in his hand, a favourite figure in opera and temple festivals.

name: Ao Guang
role: Dragon King of the Eastern Sea
fun_fact: Ao Guang's underwater palace is a treasury in myth, and his staff becomes Sun Wukong's most famous weapon.

name: Sun Wukong
role: Stone-born monkey who became the Great Sage Equal to Heaven
fun_fact: Sun Wukong can travel 108,000 li on a single somersault cloud, a distance tied to Buddhist cosmology in the novel.
